links.outcome: Readability (FKGL) of LLM responses versus physician-authored responses
links.effect: Larger models (GPT-5, Claude) reached FKGL up to 16.91-17.60 versus 11.47-12.50 for physician responses. Empathy prompting lowered FKGL by up to 6.87 points for GPT-5.
links.quote: Baseline models amplify affective polarity relative to physicians (Very Negative: 43.14-45.10% vs. 37.25%) and, in larger architectures such as GPT-5 and Claude, produce substantially higher linguistic complexity (FKGL up to 16.91-17.60 vs. 11.47-12.50 in physician-authored responses).

links.outcome: Affective polarity and empathy of LLM responses compared with physicians
links.effect: Baseline LLMs had more Very Negative affect (43.14-45.10% vs. 37.25% for physicians). Empathy-oriented prompting reduced extreme negativity without significantly raising semantic fidelity.
links.quote: Baseline models amplify affective polarity relative to physicians (Very Negative: 43.14-45.10% vs. 37.25%) and, in larger architectures such as GPT-5 and Claude, produce substantially higher linguistic complexity (FKGL up to 16.91-17.60 vs. 11.47-12.50 in physician-authored responses).
